arxiv-2104-08143.title: Efficient space-time adaptivity for parabolic evolution equations using wavelets in time and finite elements in space Thanks: Funding: Both authors are supported by the Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research (NWO) under contract. no. 613.001.652
arxiv-2104-08143.creator: Raymond van Venetië and Jan Westerdiep
arxiv-2104-08143.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Raymond van Venetië and Jan Westerdiep. Considering the space-time adaptive method for parabolic evolution equations introduced in [arXiv:2101.03956 [math.NA]], this work discusses an implementation of the method in which every step is of linear complexity. Exploiting the product structure of the space-time cylinder, the method allows for a family of trial spaces given as the spans of wavelets-in-time tensorized with (locally refined) finite element spaces-in-space.

arxiv-2105-08380.title: Well-posedness and Continuity Properties of the Degasperis-Procesi equation in critical Besov space
arxiv-2105-08380.creator: Jinlu Li, Yanghai Yu, Weipeng Zhu
arxiv-2105-08380.description: Abstract Abstract: In this paper, we obtain the local-in-time existence and uniqueness of solution to the Degasperis-Procesi equation in B^{1}_{\infty,1}(\mathbb{R}) . Moreover, we prove that the data-to-solution of this equation is continuous but not uniformly continuous in B^{1}_{\infty,1} . Keywords: Degasperis-Procesi equation; Local well-posedness; non-uniform dependence MSC (2010): 35Q53, 37K10.

arxiv-2205-03852.title: Randomized geometric tools for anomaly detection in stock markets
arxiv-2205-03852.creator: Cyril Bachelard, Apostolos Chalkis, Vissarion Fisikopoulos, Elias Tsigaridas
arxiv-2205-03852.description: Abstract We propose novel randomized geometric tools to detect low-volatility anomalies in stock markets; a principal problem in financial economics. Our modeling of the (detection) problem results in sampling and estimating the (relative) volume of geodesically non-convex and non-connected spherical patches that arise by intersecting a non-standard simplex with a sphere.

arxiv-2402-05486.title: Gravitating kinks with asymptotically flat metrics
arxiv-2402-05486.creator: Ziqi Wang, Yuan Zhong, Hui Wang
arxiv-2402-05486.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ziqi Wang, Yuan Zhong, Hui Wang. In this work, we consider a two-dimensional (2D) dilaton gravity model where the dilaton kinetic term 𝒳 \mathcal{X} is modified by an additional derivative coupling term α ​ 𝒳 2 \alpha\mathcal{X}^{2} . In the case with a canonical scalar matter field, the field equations of this model have a simple first-order formalism, from which exact static kink solutions can be constructed.

arxiv-2404-08854.title: gnss_lib_py: Analyzing GNSS Data with Python Journal: SoftwareX
arxiv-2404-08854.creator: Derek Knowles, Ashwin Vivek Kanhere, Daniel Neamati, Grace Gao
arxiv-2404-08854.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Derek Knowles, Ashwin Vivek Kanhere, Daniel Neamati, Grace Gao. This paper presents gnss_lib_py , a Python library used to parse, analyze, and visualize data from a variety of GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite Systems) data sources. The gnss_lib_py library’s ease of use, modular capabilities, testing coverage, and extensive documentation make it an attractive tool not only for scientific and industry users wanting a quick, out-of-the-box solution but also for advanced GNSS users developing new GNSS algorithms.

arxiv-2405-12654.title: Utilizing Description Logics for Global Explanations of Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks
arxiv-2405-12654.creator: Dominik Köhler, Stefan Heindorf
arxiv-2405-12654.description: Abstract . Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are effective for node classification in graph-structured data, but they lack explainability, especially at the global level. Current research mainly utilizes subgraphs of the input as local explanations or generates new graphs as global explanations. However, these graph-based methods are limited in their ability to explain classes with multiple sufficient explanations.

arxiv-2409-20237.title: Classroom-Inspired Multi-Mentor Distillation with Adaptive Learning Strategies
arxiv-2409-20237.creator: Shalini Sarode 1 2, Muhammad Saif Ullah Khan 1 2 ⋆, Tahira Shehzadi 1 2, Didier Stricker 1 2, Muhammad Zeshan Afzal 1 2
arxiv-2409-20237.description: Abstract We propose ClassroomKD , a novel multi-mentor knowledge distillation framework inspired by classroom environments to enhance knowledge transfer between the student and multiple mentors with different knowledge levels. Unlike traditional methods that rely on fixed mentor-student relationships, our framework dynamically selects and adapts the teaching strategies of diverse mentors based on their effectiveness for each data sample.

arxiv-2602-22924.title: Refined wave breaking for the generalized Fornberg-Whitham equation
arxiv-2602-22924.creator: Jean-Claude Saut, and Yuexun Wang
arxiv-2602-22924.description: Abstract . This paper considers a class of non-local equations that are weakly dispersive perturbations of the inviscid Burgers equation, which includes the Fornberg-Whitham equation as a special case. We precise the known results on finite time blow-up (shock formation) by constructing a blowup solution which displays a ‘shock-like’ singularity (called wave breaking) at one single point.

pmc-10551172.title: Does rDLPFC activity alter trust? Evidence from a tDCS study
pmc-10551172.creator: Letian Sun, Xinbo Lu, Haoli Zheng, Lulu Zeng, Wanjun Zheng, Jinjin Wang
pmc-10551172.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Trust plays an important role in the human economy and people’s social lives. Trust is affected by various factors and is related to many brain regions, such as the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC). However, few studies have focused on the impact of the DLPFC on trust through transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), although abundant psychology and neuroscience studies have theoretically discussed the possible link between DLPFC activity and trust.

pmc-11101200.title: Plastic, It’s What’s for Dinner: A Preliminary Comparison of Ingested Particles in Bottlenose Dolphins and Their Prey
pmc-11101200.creator: Leslie B. Hart, Miranda Dziobak, Randall S. Wells, Elizabeth Berens McCabe, Eric Conger, Tita Curtin, Maggie Knight, John Weinstein
pmc-11101200.description: Microplastic ingestion was reported for common bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops truncatus) inhabiting Sarasota Bay, FL, USA, a community that also has prevalent exposure to plasticizers (i.e., phthalates) at concentrations higher than human reference populations. Exposure sources are currently unknown, but plastic-contaminated prey could be a vector.

pmc-11427320.title: Oral microbiome diversity shapes the association between sleep duration and depression
pmc-11427320.creator: Yan Liu, Ling Zhang, Can Yang, Liping Zhi, Xu Steven Xu, Min Yuan
pmc-11427320.description: BackgroundEmerging research suggests the relationship between the oral microbiome and sleep duration with depression, however, the precise mechanisms by which oral microbial diversity influences the sleep-depression nexus remain to be elucidated.MethodsWe analyzed data from 4,692 participants in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), incorporating key demographic variables, oral microbiome diversity metrics, sleep duration, and depression assessment variables.

pmc-11439532.title: Non-encapsidated miRNA contaminants found in AAV preparations
pmc-11439532.creator: Mark A Brimble, Stephen M Winston
pmc-11439532.description: there has been extensive work profiling and understanding the unintended DNA molecules contained within preparations of AAV.2 This has increased awareness of the causes of these DNA impurities and innovation to minimize their encapsidation within AAV particles. In a new article, Penaud-Budloo and colleagues examine a previously unexplored consideration: the RNA content of recombinant AAV (rAAV) preparations.

pmc-11506793.title: Brain-Inspired Architecture for Spiking Neural Networks
pmc-11506793.creator: Fengzhen Tang, Junhuai Zhang, Chi Zhang, Lianqing Liu
pmc-11506793.description: Spiking neural networks (SNNs), using action potentials (spikes) to represent and transmit information, are more biologically plausible than traditional artificial neural networks. However, most of the existing SNNs require a separate preprocessing step to convert the real-valued input into spikes that are then input to the network for processing.

pmc-11677811.title: Pharmacogenetics of Neoadjuvant MAP Chemotherapy in Localized Osteosarcoma: A Study Based on Data from the GEIS-33 Protocol
pmc-11677811.creator: Juliana Salazar, María J. Arranz, Javier Martin-Broto, Francisco Bautista, Jerónimo Martínez-García, Javier Martínez-Trufero, Yolanda Vidal-Insua, Aizpea Echebarria-Barona, Roberto Díaz-Beveridge, Claudia Valverde, Pablo Luna, María A. Vaz-Salgado, Pilar Blay, Rosa Álvarez, Ana Sebio
pmc-11677811.description: Background: Osteosarcoma is a rare disease, but it is the most frequent malignant bone tumor. Primary treatment consists of preoperative MAP (methotrexate (MTX), doxorubicin and cisplatin) chemotherapy followed by surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy. Pathological response to preoperative chemotherapy is one of the most important prognostic factors, but molecular biomarkers are lacking. Additionally, chemotherapy-induced toxicity might jeopardize treatment completion.

pmc-12553518.title: A Case Report of Spontaneous Unilateral Adrenal Hemorrhage in the Third Trimester of Pregnancy
pmc-12553518.creator: Man Wai Cheng, Khurram Khan
pmc-12553518.description: This case report describes a 33-year-old woman who developed spontaneous adrenal hemorrhage during the third trimester of pregnancy. She presented with left upper quadrant abdominal pain, which was described as pleuritic in nature, with shortness of breath. She also described nausea and had been sick a couple of times before she came to the hospital.

pmc-13560254.title: Virobiome-mediated regulation of microbiota–gut–brain axis signaling and neuroimmune homeostasis
pmc-13560254.creator: Alireza Afkhamian, Abolfazl Saffari Natanzi, Mahin Jafaridarabjerdi, Sara Aghaei, Ali Haghjou, Mohammadreza Shafiei, Aysa Hasanzade Bashkandi, Sajjad Shahraki, Russel J Reiter, Hamed Haddad Kashani, Yanchao Yang
pmc-13560254.description: The human gut-brain axis (GBA) is increasingly recognized as a complex bidirectional communication system integrating microbial, neural, endocrine, and immune networks that shape neurological health. While bacterial contributions to this dialogue have been extensively characterized, the viral component of the gut ecosystem, the virome, has emerged as an important component associated with host physiological regulation.

uslaw-usc-t23-s164.description: United States Code, Title 23 (Highways); Chapter 1 (Federal-Aid Highways). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Definitions.— In this section, the following definitions apply: (1) 24-7 sobriety program.— The term “24-7 sobriety program” has the meaning given the term in section 405(d)(7)(A). (2) Alcohol concentration.— The term “alcohol concentration” means grams of alcohol per 100 milliliters of blood or grams of alcohol.

uslaw-usc-t42-s300n3.title: 42 U.S.C. § 300n–3 — Technical assistance and provision of supplies and services in lieu of grant funds
uslaw-usc-t42-s300n3.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s300n3.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 6A (Public Health Service); Subchapter XIII (Preventive Health Measures With Respect To Breast And Cervical Cancers). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Technical assistance The Secretary may provide training and technical assistance with respect to the planning, development, and operation of any program or service carried out pursuant to section 300k.
